source_refs.note: Exercise 4.1, Question 5: radioactive decay (Hint); book p. 128, answers p. 303 (PDF 305)

blocks.prompt: 5 Let \(N\) denote the amount of radioactive substance present at time \(t\). Construct a differential equation that models the radioactive decay of the substance. Hint: (Radioactive decay is a natural process by which an unstable atomic nucleus loses energy by emitting radiation. The rate at which a radioactive substance decays is proportional to the amount of the substance present at any given time.)
blocks.explanation:
Yeh model banane ka sawal hai, aur hint ne aadha kaam kar diya hai: decay ka rate maujooda miqdaar \(N\) ke proportional hai.
Diya kya hai? Radioactive cheez ki miqdaar \(N\) time \(t\) par.
Find kya karna hai? \(N\) ke liye differential equation.
Decay ka matlab \(N\) ghat raha hai, is liye \(\frac{dN}{dt}\) negative hoga; isi se sign tay hoga.
steps:
Diya gaya: miqdaar \(N(t)\); decay ka rate \(N\) ke proportional.
Maloom karna: \(N\) ke liye differential equation.
Tareeqa: decay model \(\frac{dN}{dt} = -kN\), jahan \(k > 0\).

Proportionality likhiye
\[\dfrac{dN}{dt} \propto N\]
Kyun: jitne zyada atoms, utne zyada har second toot'te hain. Jaise ek bare dher mein se zyada daane girte hain aur chhote dher mein se kam.

Sign tay kijiye
\(N\) ghat raha hai, is liye \(\frac{dN}{dt} < 0\). Positive constant \(k\) (decay constant) ke saath:
\[\dfrac{dN}{dt} = -kN\]
\[\dfrac{dN}{dt} + kN = 0,\quad k > 0\]
Kyun: yeh Example 1 ka model \(\frac{dP}{dt} = kP\) hi hai, bas constant negative hai, aur kitab ki Observation ise decay kehti hai.
Dhyan dein: yahan variable \(N\) hai; right side par bhi \(N\) hi aayega, koi aur harf nahi.
Is sawal mein shayad aap ne answer key mein \(-kT\) dekha ho; woh chhapai ki ghalti hai (neeche dekhiye). Har model mein right side par wohi variable aata hai jis ka rate left side par hai.

Tasdeeq:
\(N = N_{0}e^{-kt}\) se \(\frac{dN}{dt} = -kN_{0}e^{-kt} = -kN\) (sympy); \(N\) zero ki taraf ghatta hai magar kabhi negative nahi hota, jaise asal mein hona chahiye.
blocks.final_answer: \(\dfrac{dN}{dt} = -kN\), i.e. \(\dfrac{dN}{dt} + kN = 0\), where \(k > 0\) is the decay constant.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Answer key \(\frac{dN}{dt} = -kT,\ k > 0\) likhti hai. Is sawal mein \(T\) hai hi nahi; decay ka rate miqdaar \(N\) par depend karta hai. Sahi equation \(\frac{dN}{dt} = -kN,\ k > 0\) hai.
